intro_zh: 嵩山少林风景区位于河南省登封市境内，除了巍峨耸立的嵩山，景区还有始建于北魏的少林寺、规模宏大的中岳庙、程朱理学发源地嵩阳书院等古迹。其中，少林寺有“天下第一名刹”的美誉，现存建筑包括常住院、塔林、初祖庵、二祖庵及达摩洞等。2007年8月17日，嵩山少林风景区入选首批国家5A级景区。
intro_en: Shaolin Monastery (少林寺; shàolín-sì), also known as Shaolin Temple, is a Mahayana Buddhist monastic institution associated with the development of Chan Buddhism and Shaolin kung fu. It is located at the foot of Wuru Peak of the Mount Song mountain range in Dengfeng, Zhengzhou prefecture, in Henan, China. The name reflects its location in the ancient grove (林; lín) of Mount Shaoshi, in the hinterland of the Mount Song range. Mount Song occupied was recognized as one of China's sacred mountains as early as the 1st century BC, when it was proclaimed one of the Five Holy Peaks. It is located some 48 km (30 mi) southeast of Luoyang, the former capital of the Northern Wei Dynasty (386–534), and 72 km (45 mi) southwest of Zhengzhou, the modern capital of Henan Province. The first Shaolin abbot, Batuo, translated Buddhist texts and taught Buddhist doctrines to hundreds of his followers. According to legend, Bodhidharma, the 28th patriarch of Mahayana Buddhism, arrived at the Shaolin Temple in 527 from India.
